task.question: I hold 40% NVDA, 30% MSFT, 30% AAPL — should I add 15% TSLA?
task.name: TSLA

read_as.summary: add 15% TSLA to 40% NVDA / 30% MSFT / 30% AAPL

lines: At 15%, TSLA would carry 19% of the book's risk, inside the 25% budget; 18% is the most that stays inside.
The book's concentration is NVDA, not TSLA: after the trade NVDA carries 43% of the risk at 34% of the money. If that is the worry, trimming NVDA to 23% brings it inside the 25% budget.
Fill it as 60% near-touch limit then 40% market for $15,000, about 8.8 bps all in on the live book (one market order: 10.0 bps).

What would change the call: if TSLA outruns the rest of the book by 24%, it drifts past 18% of the book and back over the budget; trim it to 15% then. A jump in its correlation with the book lowers that ceiling, so re-ask after a large move.

weighing.call: No measured edge: enter only on your own view
weighing.reason: Nothing the engines measured favours entering over waiting: from states like today's TSLA rose 74% of the time over 24 hours, median +35 bps, but 13 independent episodes cannot tell 74% from an even chance (±28% at two standard errors); the long-run daily base rate does not move either. Entering is a view you hold, not one the data gives.
disagreements: The tape says momentum is turning down (MACD histogram -0.277, 4h); the past says states like this rose — median +35 bps over 24 hours, up 74% of the time. Which to weigh: neither — the technical signals tested on these names did not clear costs, and the base rate is within chance.

questions: How long will you hold it? The call above reads the next 24 hours; over 20 trading days states like this rose 57% of the time, against 55% for any day — the horizon changes the answer.
What loss on this position would you accept? The sizing assumed the default 25% risk budget.
Where would you be wrong? Its worst 24 hours in the data was -2.0% — an exit decided now is one a move cannot talk you out of.

steps.title: What the trade does to your book
steps.engine: your book's risk on 30 days of hourly returns
lines: Bottom line: to keep TSLA under 25% of book risk, size it at no more than 18% — the 15% proposed is inside that budget.
At 15% of the book, TSLA would carry 19% of your total risk.
Open-session beta 0.86 → 0.94
Risk spread across 2.6 → 3.4 effective position(s)
Most correlated with NVDA at +0.28; largely a different bet from what you already own
Hedge: short QQQ worth about 94% of the book's value neutralises its market exposure (book beta 0.94); it does nothing for single-name news risk.
After the trade: NVDA 34% weight / 43% risk; AAPL 26% weight / 22% risk; TSLA 15% weight / 19% risk; MSFT 26% weight / 16% risk.
In the book's worst 5% of hours (an average loss of 0.38% an hour), TSLA would carry 15% of the loss, against 19% of the ordinary swing.
If QQQ falls 5%, the book moves about -4.7% through beta alone.
If QQQ falls 10%, the book moves about -9.4% through beta alone.
Realised worst case: the worst 24-bar window in the observed history would have moved this book -2.05% — driven by TSLA -7.83%, MSFT -1.94%, AAPL -1.81%
Sectors after the trade (Yahoo's classification, GICS names): Information Technology 100% → 85%, Consumer Discretionary 0% → 15%.

Factor loadings before → after (daily regression on SPY, IWM minus SPY, MTUM minus SPY, VLUE minus SPY, QUAL minus SPY, USMV minus SPY, IEF and BTC): market 1.08 → 1.15, size -0.22 → -0.16, momentum -0.20 → -0.17, value -0.28 → -0.28, quality -0.18 → -0.41, low vol -0.57 → -0.57, rates -0.28 → -0.27, crypto 0.01 → 0.03. Ask "what are my exposures" for the t-statistics.

How far to trust that beta: on 1,800 test books, it missed the next four weeks' realised beta by 0.24 on average. weekend-copilot, an S2 entry answering this same question, missed by 0.55 as it ships (p = 0.01) and by 0.36 on the same benchmark (p = 0.10, not significant); simply assuming a beta of 1.0 missed by 0.30. The QQQ-fall lines were off by 0.92 points on the 39 days QQQ really fell 1% or more (skfolio's vine copula: 1.00), and they are a centre, not a worst case

Assumed: loadings fitted over the last 252 US trading days available (2025-09-25 to 2026-09-25, 252 daily returns per holding), all 8 factors at once; |t| above 2 is a loading the data pins down, below 2 one it cannot tell from zero.

TSLA's daily correlation +0.44 with the rest of the book over 252 shared days: it moves partly apart from what you hold.

Data: sectors from data/sector_map.json (Yahoo quoteSummary, frozen 2026-09-25); factor returns from SPY, IWM, MTUM, VLUE, QUAL, USMV and IEF daily closes (Yahoo) and BTCUSDT daily candles (Bitget, 16:00 UTC close, four hours before the US close); holdings from AAPL daily closes (Yahoo); MSFT daily closes (Yahoo); NVDA daily closes (Yahoo); TSLA daily closes (Yahoo).

Method: one least-squares regression per holding of its daily returns on SPY, IWM minus SPY, MTUM minus SPY, VLUE minus SPY, QUAL minus SPY, USMV minus SPY, IEF and BTC together; the book's loading is the weight-sum of its holdings' (argus.lui.exposures).

steps.title: How to execute the size
lines: Bottom line: in one market order this costs about 10.0bps (6.0bps fee + 4.0bps book impact) — enough book impact that splitting on the schedule below is worth doing.

A $15,000 order is 0.90% of TSLA's 24h volume ($1,665,231); the fees come to about 6.0bps, and the square-root impact law — calibrated on Bitget's own books, at TSLA's own 252bps daily volatility — puts this size's market impact near 8.2bps; the live book below shows what taking it at once costs.
Plan: the stock's own market is shut, so this book is thin and resting orders tend to fill only when the price moves against them — passive orders get less of the size, not more.
Order book (buy side, live): taking all $15,000 at once walks 18 level(s) for 4.0bps of slippage on top of the fee.
Slice 1: 60% ($9,000) as near-touch limit — about 6.0bps fee plus 3.1bps book impact.
Slice 2: 40% ($6,000) as market — about 6.0bps fee plus 2.4bps book impact.

Schedule (Almgren-Chriss optimum, inventory decaying e-fold over 3 hour(s)): trade 39%, 32%, 29% of $15,000 hour by hour — expected cost 8.2bps with a one-standard-deviation risk of ±6.8bps, against 8.2bps ± 7.5bps for an even split, with the slice styles above applied inside each hour. Impact is priced from sweeping one hour's share of the order on the live book.

Worst case: at 95% confidence, the schedule that keeps the cost lowest does 99% of the order in the first half, and its 95% worst case is 11.8bps against 20.5bps for an even split — read off 41 optimal schedules, cost against risk.

Cadence: send each hour's share as one-minute children, as Bitget's own TWAP does at a 60-second interval. Replaying a full day of Bitget's NVDA order book, $5,000 orders cost 6.3bps with fees in one-minute children against 7.6bps in hourly ones (Bitget's TWAP: 6.3bps; all at once: 9.4bps).

Waiting costs too: at this volatility the price drifts an expected 1.3bps in the minute between deciding and the first order landing, 4.1bps in ten — a cost of deliberating, separate from the impact above.
